sentences.zh: 那么阿里，成吉思汗，这不是正确的发音，对吧？

sentences.en: It isn't.
sentences.zh: 不是的。

sentences.en: It isn't actually.
sentences.zh: 其实并不是。

sentences.en: Well, as far as we can tell, because actually the more accurate pronunciation or rendition seems to be, and I dare say, among Persian historians of the Mongol period, and it's
sentences.zh: 嗯，据我们所知，因为实际上更准确的发音或译法似乎是——我敢说，在蒙古时期的波斯历史学家中间，它是

sentences.en: actually Cengiz, it's a C-H rather than a G.
sentences.zh: 其实是 Cengiz，开头发音是“切”而不是“盖”。

sentences.en: So people tend to agree that basically they have the nearest pronunciation or the nearest
sentences.zh: 所以人们倾向于认为，基本上他们保留了最接近的发音或者最接近的

sentences.en: The Persians did?
sentences.zh: 波斯人保留了？

sentences.en: Yes, because they – So you're saying the Persians pronounced it better than the Mongols?
sentences.zh: 是的，因为他们——所以你是说波斯人比蒙古人发音更标准？

sentences.en: Yeah, Persian historians are really the ones that we can't do without, because a number of Persian historians, and one of them in particular who I'll be quoting pretty liberally
sentences.zh: 对，波斯历史学家确实是我们不可或缺的，因为许多波斯历史学家，其中一位我将在整期节目中大量引用，

sentences.en: throughout here, was one of the ones who actually went to Karakorum and actually looked at the secret history and was actually invited to write a sort of a –
sentences.zh: 他是那些真正去过哈喇和林、看过《蒙古秘史》并被邀请去撰写某种——的人之一。

sentences.en: So tell us about the secret history, because we should probably discuss the – I mean,
sentences.zh: 给我们讲讲《蒙古秘史》吧，因为我们可能应该讨论一下——我的意思是，

sentences.en: Tom, we're not a PhD.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我们又不是博士。

sentences.en: We should have a chapter on sources to start the podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我们在播客开头应该专门搞一章来讲讲资料来源。

sentences.en: So you're going to be citing Persian sources, but the secret – I mean, the secret history is great, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以你要引用波斯资料，但《蒙古秘史》——我的意思是，《蒙古秘史》很棒，对吧？

sentences.en: Because that's the Mongolian form.
sentences.zh: 因为那是蒙古本土的形式。

sentences.en: The secret history is great, but the only accounts we have, or the only versions we have left are actually taken from Chinese chronicles.
sentences.zh: 《蒙古秘史》很棒，但我们拥有的唯一记载，或者说仅存的版本，其实都是取自中国史书。

sentences.en: So the Chinese basically translated it, it's in the Chinese chronicles, and then it's been retranslated back.
sentences.zh: 所以中国人基本上把它翻译了过去，它被收录在中国史书中，然后又被重新翻译回来。

sentences.en: The other sources we have for the secret history are basically a number of Persian historians,
sentences.zh: 我们关于《蒙古秘史》的其他资料基本上来自多位波斯历史学家，

sentences.en: particularly this gentleman known as Juveni, who travelled to Karakorum and actually is claimed to have seen it.
sentences.zh: 特别是这位名叫志费尼（Juveni）的绅士，他曾前往哈喇和林，据称还亲眼见过它。

sentences.en: So what we can do is compare these two different sources and see what they tell us about the early life of Genghis Khan.
sentences.zh: 所以我们可以做的是，对比这两种不同的资料来源，看看它们向我们讲述了成吉思汗早年生活的什么情况。

sentences.en: And, you know, there's a sort of a – you know, they sort of – they echo each other.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，有一种——你知道，它们某种程度上——它们彼此呼应。

sentences.en: So just a couple of things, Ali, before we get started.
sentences.zh: 阿里，在我们开始之前，还有几件事要说。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 请讲。

sentences.en: So first of all, we are in – for those people who don't know, we are in the medieval period.
sentences.zh: 首先，对于那些不知道的人来说，我们正处于中世纪时期。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: We kick off in the 12th century, and he dies in the 13th century.
sentences.zh: 我们从12世纪开始，他死于13世纪。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And he is the person who is the architect, the initial – the founding father of this kind of huge period of Mongol expansion, I guess.
sentences.zh: 他是这种庞大的蒙古扩张时期的缔造者、最初的——国父，我猜。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The most sort of rapid expansion probably in human history.
sentences.zh: 这可能是人类历史上最迅速的扩张。

sentences.en: Now, the second thing I was going to say is you talked about his name, Genghis, but that's not his original name, right?
sentences.zh: 现在，我要说的第二件事是，你刚才提到了他的名字“成吉思”，但这并不是他原本的名字，对吧？

sentences.en: No, no, that's a title.
sentences.zh: 不，不，那是一个称号。

sentences.en: It's an honorific.
sentences.zh: 这是一个尊称。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's an honorific.
sentences.zh: 对，是一个尊称。

sentences.en: And you read various – I mean, I was always taught, I have to say, and I'm going to stick with this, that Genghis Khan actually means lord of all those who dwell in felt tents.
sentences.zh: 你读过各种——我的意思是，我过去一直被教导，而且我打算坚持这个观点，成吉思汗实际上意为“住在毡房里所有人的领主”。

sentences.en: So this is an honorific that he gets in 1206 when he basically brings the Mongol confederation,
sentences.zh: 所以这是他在1206年基本上将蒙古各部、

sentences.en: the tribes together, and begins the jolly of, you know, heading down into what is now China.
sentences.zh: 各个部落统一起来，并开始带兵南下进入现今中国境内时获得的尊称。

sentences.en: And just to be clear, his surname is not Khan.
sentences.zh: 顺便明确一下，他的姓氏不是汗。

sentences.en: No, no, not at all.
sentences.zh: 不，不，完全不是。

sentences.en: Again, lord, that's lord.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，那是领主的意思。

sentences.en: Yeah, lord.
sentences.zh: 对，领主。

sentences.en: And it is one of the great banes, yes, that a lot of people tend to use Khan, because
sentences.zh: 这也是一大痛点，对吧，很多人往往会用“汗”，因为

sentences.en: Khan is also a term that's used in Persian quite frequently just to mean mister these days.
sentences.zh: 在波斯语中，“汗”如今也经常被用作“先生”的意思。

sentences.en: It's sort of slightly been diminished over the time.
sentences.zh: 随着时间推移，它的含义有些贬值了。

sentences.en: There's a lot of words that come in and seep in.
sentences.zh: 有很多词汇渗入并融入了进来。

sentences.en: But in those days, obviously, it means lord.
sentences.zh: 但在当年，显然它意味着领主。

sentences.en: But his real name is Temujin.
sentences.zh: 但他的真名叫铁木真。

sentences.en: Temujin, blacksmith.
sentences.zh: 铁木真，铁匠。

sentences.en: So he's smith.
sentences.zh: 所以他是个铁匠。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 对，对，对。

sentences.en: Before he becomes Khan, he's Mr. Smith.
sentences.zh: 在他成为大汗之前，他是史密斯先生。

sentences.en: Mr. Smith.
sentences.zh: 史密斯先生。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's a fairly...
sentences.zh: 对，这相当……

sentences.en: I mean, the interesting thing about his rise, by the way, is that quite apart from the fact that, you know, what we know comes from essentially one source.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，关于他的崛起，有趣的一点在于，抛开我们所知的内容基本上来自单一来源这一点不谈，

sentences.en: And it's pretty vague, and it's quite speculative.
sentences.zh: 而且它相当模糊，也有很多推测。

sentences.en: But it's not smooth, is what the...
sentences.zh: 但这并不顺利，正如……

sentences.en: I mean, you look at...
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你看看……

sentences.en: So you would imagine the secret history is, on the whole, quite eulogistic.
sentences.zh: 所以你会以为《蒙古秘史》总体上是一部赞美诗。

sentences.en: It obviously says, you know, what a splendid chap he was, and, you know, how he outmaneuvered all his foes.
sentences.zh: 它显然会说，你看，他是个多么了不起的家伙，你看他是如何智胜所有敌人的。

sentences.en: But it has to be said that he had a pretty rough time growing up.
sentences.zh: 但必须承认，他在成长过程中度过了一段相当艰难的时期。

sentences.en: I mean, it wasn't all easy.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，一切并非一帆风顺。

sentences.en: So Ali, before we come to Genghis Khan himself, just the background.
sentences.zh: 那么阿里，在我们聊到成吉思汗本人之前，先谈谈背景。

sentences.en: So the secret history says about the Mongols, that they are descended from a deer and a blue-grey wolf.
sentences.zh: 《蒙古秘史》里说蒙古人是鹿和青灰色狼的后代。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: There's a long line of descent, that at some point, there's a mysterious glowing man who appears through a tent, and he contributes to the bloodline of the Mongols.
sentences.zh: 这里有一长串血统传承，在某个时候，一个神秘的发光男子穿过帐篷出现，他为蒙古人的血统贡献了一份力量。

sentences.en: But they are basically, when Temujin is born into them, they're a fairly insignificant tribe on the Mongolian steppes.
sentences.zh: 但当铁木真出生时，他们基本上只是蒙古草原上的一个无足轻重的部落。

sentences.en: Well, basically, I mean, the Mongols, yeah, there are a number of different tribes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，基本上，我的意思是，蒙古人，对，有许多不同的部落。

sentences.en: I mean, basically, on the, you know, what we consider to be the outer hinterland of the
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，基本上在，你知道，我们认为的中国帝国的外部腹地，

sentences.en: Chinese sort of imperium, what is now, basically, I suppose, you know, Mongolia and that sort of outer area of Siberia.
sentences.zh: 也就是现在基本上，我想，你知道，蒙古以及西伯利亚的外围地区。

sentences.en: And there are a number of different tribes who are basically, you know, designated as a part of a sort of a Mongol confederation.
sentences.zh: 那里有许多不同的部落，基本上，你知道，被指定为某种蒙古部落联盟的一部分。

sentences.en: I don't think you can devise them as one people.
sentences.zh: 我不认为你能把他们看作是一个单一的民族。

sentences.en: I mean, this is the interesting thing, is that what Temujin does is he basically welds them into a single group.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有趣的地方就在于此，铁木真所做的就是把他们融合成了一个单一的群体。

sentences.en: He's not the first person to do it.
sentences.zh: 他不是第一个这么做的人。

sentences.en: I mean, there have been threats before, and the Chinese deal with them in various ways, either through bribery or defeats and this sort of thing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，以前也有过威胁，中国通过各种方式应对他们，或是通过贿赂，或是通过击败等等。

sentences.en: What, what actually Temujin does, aka Genghis Khan, is basically not only wield them into a hole, if I can put it that way, but then ensure they have someone else to fight.
sentences.zh: 铁木真，也就是成吉思汗，实际上所做的不仅是将他们凝聚成一个整体（如果我这么说的话），而且还确保他们有其他人可以去攻打。

sentences.en: I mean, that's, that's the other thing.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，那个，这也是关键所在。

sentences.en: So he directs them elsewhere, and that keeps them all united, unified.
sentences.zh: 所以他把他们的矛头指向了别处，这让他们保持了团结、凝聚力。

sentences.en: Just before we start on his, on Temujin's actual career, the context for this, so you said that these are tribes who are nomadic.
sentences.zh: 在我们开始讲述他——铁木真的实际经历之前，先说一下背景，你刚才说过这些都是游牧部落。

sentences.en: They live beyond the bounds of the Chinese empire.
sentences.zh: 他们生活在中国帝国的边界之外。

sentences.en: So the Great Wall is basically, you know, the various incarnations of the Great Wall.
sentences.zh: 所以万里长城基本上就是，你知道，万里长城的各种化身。

sentences.en: Various incarnations of it, yeah, it's not quite.
sentences.zh: 各种化身，对，差不多吧。

sentences.en: And they belong, they belong to the, the steppes.
sentences.zh: 他们属于，他们属于草原。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Which are obviously not, you know, things that you go up if the lift's not working.
sentences.zh: 显然，这可不是电梯坏了时你走上去的那种“台阶”。

sentences.en: They are huge, great plains.
sentences.zh: 它们是广袤无垠的大平原。

sentences.en: Great plains.
sentences.zh: 大平原。

sentences.en: Great grasslands, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 大草原，对吧？

sentences.en: And they basically, they extend from the Pacific right the way up to Hungary.
sentences.zh: 它们基本上从太平洋一直延伸到匈牙利。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So this is the key thing to understand, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 所以这是需要理解的关键点，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, in ecological terms, yes.
